page: Microsoft Azure L64as_v3 is a storage and memory-focused virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 512 GB of system memory, providing 8 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it bundles a massive 16,015 GB NVMe SSD, which is Premium Storage capable, while omitting any dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong multi-core processing and memory subsystem performance. The server achieves top-tier results in PassMark memory tests and strong performance in multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU suites. Cryptographic and compression operations are highly efficient, supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is exceptionally high at 4164.3 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write operations fall into the average tier.

Given its massive 16 TB local NVMe storage and high memory capacity, the L64as_v3 delivers excellent qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense, I/O-heavy workloads without requiring external storage attachments. It is highly optimized for large-scale database operations, high-throughput Redis deployments, software compilation, and data-intensive processing. However, the lack of AVX-512 support and dedicated GPUs makes it less suitable for heavy vector-based AI training or GPU-accelerated rendering tasks.
description: The Microsoft Azure L64as_v3 is a high-capacity, storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs running at 3.525 GHz and 512 GB of RAM, this instance is designed for demanding, data-intensive workloads. It comes bundled with a massive 16,015 GB local NVMe SSD, offering exceptional storage density and high-speed local I/O. Benchmark results highlight top-tier memory performance and strong multi-core processing capabilities, making it highly efficient for database operations, Redis caching, and software compilation. While it lacks dedicated GPU hardware and AVX-512 support, its balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local storage provide excellent qualitative cost efficiency for enterprise database and transactional workloads.
